module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 688
*Reference:*
- [erdosproblems.com/688](https://www.erdosproblems.com/688)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, _A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory_. Ann. Discrete Math. (1980), 89-115.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Real Filter

namespace Erdos688

/--
Define $\epsilon_n$ to be maximal such that there exists some choice of congruence class $a_p$
for all primes $n^{\epsilon_n} < p \leq n$ such that every integer in $[1,n]$ satisfies at least
one of the congruences $\equiv a_p \pmod p$.
-/
def Erdos688Prop (n : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (a : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → m ≤ n →
    ∃ (p : ℕ), p.Prime ∧ (n : ℝ)^ε < p ∧ p ≤ n ∧
      a p ≡ m [MOD p]

noncomputable def epsilonFunction (n : ℕ) : ℝ := sSup {ε : ℝ | Erdos688Prop n ε}

/--
Estimate $\epsilon_n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_688.parts.i :
    epsilonFunction =Θ[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
In particular, is it true that $\epsilon_n = o(1)$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_688.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    epsilonFunction =o[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (1 : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős claims in [Er80] (p. 106) that it is not difficult to prove
$\epsilon_n \gg \frac{\log\log\log n}{\log\log n}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_688.variants.lglglg_over_lglg_is_big_o :
    (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (log (log (log (n : ℝ)))) / (log (log (n : ℝ))))
      =O[atTop] epsilonFunction := by
  sorry

end Erdos688

could_not_verify: Erdos688.erdos_688.parts.ii: The Lean right-hand side correctly expresses epsilonFunction n → 0, but I could not independently recover the formula in the website’s “in particular” question. Direct access and /latex/688 were blocked, and the accessible reader copy omitted mathematical expressions. The original survey, p. 106, confirms the extremal construction and lower bound but does not explicitly state this little-o question.
review.notes: No mathematical defect was established. The covering quantifiers, asymptotic estimate, and lower-bound direction agree with the available source text. Independent, sorry-free checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean establish 0 ≤ epsilonFunction n ≤ 1, its values 0 at n = 0, 1, 2, normalization of residue representatives, and invariance of all three asymptotic relations under finite boundary changes. They also prove that the big-O variant is equivalent to an eventual lower bound with a positive constant. Finite covering searches through n = 13 supplied additional boundary checks. The accessible source and database still record the problem as open; the survey records the lower bound as known. One source-access limitation remains below.
